title: Ethiopian Shiro with Kibbeh
community: Ethiopian non-fasting kitchens — the enriched shiro
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Shiro with Kibbeh — Shiro Wat enriched with a generous spoonful of kibbeh stirred in at the end. The non-fasting-day version of Shiro — the kibbeh transforms the already excellent chickpea stew into something extraordinary.
longDesc: Shiro with kibbeh is the non-fasting version of Ethiopia's most practical dish — the addition of kibbeh's spiced, rich, aromatic butter turns Shiro Wat from excellent into exceptional. This is how Shiro is served at Ethiopian celebration meals when fasting is not in effect.
steps: Make Shiro Wat as per ETH102.
When cooked through and thick, remove from heat.
Stir in kibbeh. The kibbeh melts into the hot shiro.
chefTips: Add kibbeh off the heat — it should melt gently, not fry.
A generous spoon of kibbeh completely changes the character of the shiro.
commonMistakes: Adding kibbeh too early — it burns.
cookingScience: The kibbeh's spice infusion (see ETH092) combines with the shiro's chickpea base — the fat-soluble aromatic compounds from the kibbeh distribute throughout the smooth shiro, creating a unified flavour more complex than either alone.
sustainabilityTips: The kibbeh addition turns a fasting dish into a celebration dish — flexibility is the principle.
reheating: Gently — stir in fresh kibbeh after reheating for best result.
culturalNote: Shiro with kibbeh is the difference between the fasting table and the celebration table — the same dish, transformed by one spoonful of butter. It demonstrates how Ethiopian cooking uses the same building blocks for both restriction and abundance.
